messages: Anya: Quick sync — sketching a compact control for pool selection that combines min/max steppers with a small 'burst' toggle. Main goals: reduce vertical space on the capacity card, make burst obvious but not primary, and keep SLO slider + guardrail visible. Thoughts? Devin: Love the compact idea. Two quick concerns: 1) how do we surface the effective concurrency when burst is on? 2) keyboard/aria for the burst toggle needs to be explicit. Raj: From infra side — if burst is separate (toggle + extra numeric field) we need clear semantics for autoscaler: is burst additive to max or an override? Prefer additive but need to ensure rollbacks on capacity shortage. Sarah: Accessibility nits: the min/max steppers currently don't announce when the paired SLO guardrail triggers. Screen reader users need a clear live region stating 'SLO guardrail engaged: lowering burst to preserve latency'. Also color contrast on the burst pill is low — +2pt contrast needed. Mike: UX/ML note — customers expect burst to be fast but short-lived. Suggest label 'burst (short-lived)' and a tooltip: 'Extra instances for short spikes, auto-retracted when idle'. That sets expectations and avoids misunderstandings about billing. Devin: Mocked up a compact row: [Pool picker v] Min [-] 2 [+] Max [-] 8 [+] [Burst: ⦿ +2] SLO slider (ms) [guardrail badge]. My idea: keep burst visually grouped with max, slightly smaller font, and a subtle divider. Anya: Nice. Copy tweak request: change 'Burst' tooltip to 'Burst capacity (temporary) — billed while active'. We have legal & billing teams who want 'billed while active' explicit. Raj: Implementation detail: if burst is additive, we need to cap total to pool hard limit. Also need an endpoint change so Dedicated pools get a separate quota field. I'll sketch API changes but want to avoid changing client UX props too much. Devin: Accessibility/keyboard example (for devs): ```html Burst enabled: +2 GPUs, expires in 5m ``` This should cover announce + keyboard toggle. Sarah: +1 on aria-live. Also ensure focus order: pool -> min -> max -> burst -> slo. If burst is hidden behind a dropdown on small screens, it must still be reachable by keyboard in a single tab path. Anya: Product decision: default burst off, suggested burst quanta shown (e.g., +1, +2), and an inline 'why burst' link. If SLO slider would be violated by enabling burst, show a yellow badge with 'might affect SLO'. Mike: For guardrails: suggest a soft stop at 'likely SLO violation', and a hard stop only if the system cannot honor the request. Soft stop should be a inline tooltip: 'May increase 99th p99 latency by ~20% for short windows'. Raj: Edge case — when switching pools with different GPU types, burst quanta semantics break (1 A100 != 1 T4). We need to normalize burst by capacity units (vGPU-equivalent) or disable burst when pool types differ. Devin: UX option: show a small unit tag next to burst: '+2 (vGPU x1.0)'. That hints at normalization. Also keep a 'preview' line: 'Estimated effective capacity: 10 GPUs (after burst)'. Sarah: Contrast & focus tests please. I'll run the axe checks on the mock and post results. Small screens: steppers should expand to full width stacked — don't hide SLO slider. Anya: Action items: Devin — update mock with the burst grouped near max and add copy per Mike/Anya. Raj — propose minimal API change notes and pool-limit cap behavior. Sarah — run a11y checks on mock and propose color tokens. Mike — write short guardrail wording for tooltip. I'll consolidate and schedule a 20-min follow-up. :thumbsup: Devin: I'll drop updated frames in Figma by EOD and include keyboard flow. Raj: I'll draft API PR description and edge-case behavior doc. Sarah: Posting a11y checklist in this thread in 10. Mike: Draft copy posted: 'Burst capacity: temporary extra capacity billed while active. May affect tail latency; use for short traffic spikes.' Anya: Thanks all — feel free to react with :eyes: when you've reviewed the new frames.
